What Is Beautiful
To You?

Rio and I are in a hard season.
I am not asking for charity —
I am asking you to let me write you something
that will outlast the moment that paid for it.

I am a poet. Right now, Rio and I need help — keeping a roof over our heads, keeping him fed and close, keeping the words alive. This is the trade I know how to make: you tell me what you love, and I will write it the poem it deserves.

Commission a Poem Read Our Story
The reason I am here

I have written words for weddings at the Ritz,
for Louis Vuitton, for the NFL.
But life does not care about credentials.

Poetry found me young and never let go. I have written poems using my typewriter as a resident artist for The Ritz-Carlton, Kimpton, and The Standard Hotel, as well as celebrity weddings, Ferragamo stores, NFL Owner meetings, Coachella, Art Basel secret events, and even warehouse techno clubs and dainty tea parties — wherever the right words at the right moment could change something in a room full of people.

Rio and I are in a hard season — the kind that doesn't announce itself until you are already inside it. I am not asking for charity. I am asking for a trade. I need help keeping a roof over our heads, keeping him fed and close. In return, I will give you something I am genuinely good at: a poem written only for you, from what you share with me.

This project — What Is Beautiful To You? — is that trade. You tell me what you love. I will write it the poem it deserves. You can also read our full story on GoFundMe →

✦

From my work

and the smallest moment
is given the dignity
of forever
— Ryan Ash-is The Poet & Rio the Phoenix

What is beautiful to you?

There are no wrong answers. Only honest ones. The more you give me, the more I can give back.

Where shall I send the physical poem? Yours or a loved one's address.
A person. A place. A season. A scent. A dog. A song. A memory that won't leave you alone. Name it — I'll find my way in.
This is the question I most want you to sit with. Not what it looks like — what it feels like. Why does it stop you? Is it a sound, a scent, the way light falls at a particular hour? A memory inside it? A loss it carries? Go as deep as you can. Let me feel your admiration from across the page. The more you trust me with, the more true the poem will be.
Yourself? A gift? Tell me the occasion if there is one, or simply who deserves these words.
A tone. A word you love or hate. A story. A date that matters. Nothing is too small.
